# Test data

Hand-built MIDI files that reach a mechanism no ordinary corpus file does. Each is small enough to
read in a hex editor and is generated by a script in `../tools/`, so the file and its recipe travel
together.

Nothing here is Roland-derived. These are our own files and can be redistributed.

## `randlfo1_*.mid` — a random LFO1 on a two-partial tone

Six files: `stream` and `bubble` at keys 48, 60 and 72, one note each with a GS reset and a bank
select in front of it.

They exist because the note sweep cannot see the shared-LFO1 node. `partial_alloc_node @ 1800029e0`
claims **one** LFO1 node per note and refcounts it by partial count, so a two-partial tone has one
LFO1 and two LFO2s. That is only observable when LFO1 is one of the three random shapes, since only
then does it draw from the shared generator — one draw per wrap for the note, not one per partial.

Twelve tones in the whole table have a random LFO1 and eight of those have two partials, and **not
one of them is reachable from any of the 185 melodic cases in the note sweep**. `Stream` and
`Bubble` are, though: they sit at bank 4 and bank 5 of program 122 on every map including the
SC-55's, so a bank select is all it takes.

Beware the waveform map when reproducing this. `header[0x0E] & 0x1f` is an index into
`g_lfo_wave_map`, and the random shapes are its entries **5, 6 and 7** — not 1, 2 and 3, which map
to ordinary geometric shapes. Scanning for the raw selector instead of the mapped one finds 43
tones, none of them random.

Regenerate with:

    python3 tools/make_randlfo1_probe.py testdata/lfo/randlfo1_stream_k60.mid 4 122 60 100
    python3 tools/make_randlfo1_probe.py testdata/lfo/randlfo1_bubble_k60.mid 5 122 60 100
